filenames = [ "filename_1", "filename_2", "filename_3" ]
# Hashes are unnecessary if comparing whole files. hashes = [ "hash_1", "hash_2", "hash_3" ] hash_dict = dict(zip(filenames, hashes))
must_have = [ "term_1", "term_2" ]
cannot_have = [ "term_3", "term_4" ]
options = { files_or_hashes: "files", filenames: correct_answers, hashes: hash_dict, "must_have": must_have, "cannot_have": cannot_have, "files_or_hashes": "files", # alternative: "hashes" "credit_options": { "blank_lines": 0.8, "case": 0.6, "spaces": 0.9, "low_cutoff": 0.5, "high_cutoff": 0.9, "participation_points": 0.2 } }
# In this problem type we're using javascript to grade. # This is not standard, so I wanted to point it out here. # It potentially reveals correct answers to tech-savvy learners. def answercheck(e, ans):
response = json.loads(ans) JSProblemState = json.loads(response["state"])
ok = "partial" if JSProblemState["final_credit"] == 1: ok = True elif JSProblemState["final_credit"] == 0: ok = False
rounded_grade = round(JSProblemState["final_credit"], 2)
return { "input_list": [ { "ok": ok, "msg": "", "grade_decimal": rounded_grade, } ] }
